content.title: About
content.content: Low‑fat buttermilk is a fermented dairy drink made from skimmed milk inoculated with a culture of lactic acid bacteria. It has a mild tangy flavor, light texture, and a reduced fat content, making it popular among those watching their calorie intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Buttermilk is traditionally considered a probiotic food that supports gut health.
Low‑fat buttermilk contains almost as much protein as regular buttermilk but roughly half the fat.
In many countries it is used as a base for cold soups such as okroshka.
Buttermilk can replace milk in baking, giving pastries a subtle tang.
Fermentation reduces the lactose content compared with plain milk.

items.title: Supports gut microbiota
items.content: Live probiotic cultures in buttermilk help promote the growth of beneficial intestinal bacteria.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The reduced‑fat version fits well into low‑fat diets and helps control overall calorie intake.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: One cup of buttermilk provides about 8 g of high‑quality protein, important for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Buttermilk supplies vitamin B12, riboflavin, and niacin, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Calcium in buttermilk supports bone and teeth health.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to buttermilk.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: Although lower than regular milk, buttermilk can still be problematic for those with severe lactose intolerance.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Some commercial buttermilk varieties contain added salt, which should be considered on low‑sodium diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Low‑fat buttermilk can be enjoyed as a drink, added to smoothies, used as a salad dressing, incorporated into pancake or waffle batter, and employed as a tenderizing marinate for meat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep buttermilk refrigerated at 1‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
